items.item_text: Associate Social Worker License issued by the California Board of Behavioral Sciences Examiners within 90 days of hire.
A Master's Degree from an accredited School of Social Work.
Experience in a social service or healthcare setting (i.e. case management or social worker).
Social Work experience in a jail or correctional setting.

The role of this position is that the Social Worker I is to plan, organize conduct a wide range of individual and group activities of a psychoeducational, social, cultural, or creative arts nature which will facilitate diagnosis, evaluation, planning, and treatment of patients receiving services from ACMH. They will provide clinical social work evaluations, counseling, monitoring of medication side effects under the direction of a Psychiatrist, and case management. Also included are pre-release planning, crisis intervention, and the maintenance of an ongoing caseload, documentation, triage, consultation, training, education and referral. Social Worker I’s (MSW I) provide services under the clinical supervision of a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW). All clinical work, documentation, assessments, treatment recommendations, and case management activities are reviewed and supervised in accordance with applicable professional standards, and organizational policies to ensure compliance and quality of care.
Demonstrated awareness of, and sensitivity to, dealings with cultural and socioeconomic diversity.
Basic understanding of computer and MS functionality.

Knowledge and understanding of individual, child, and family development, human behavior and communication, the influence of culture and values in social work practice, psychotherapy, case management, and the relation between social work practice and medicine.
Knowledge of criminal justice system, state hospital system, forensic mental healthcare, Probation, Parole, and Department of Corrections.
Knowledge and skills in the areas of individual, group, and family therapy.

Knowledge of child, elder abuse, and domestic violence reporting requirements, and other significant legislation and laws regulating social work practice, e.g., Tarasoff, patient confidentiality, etc. Ability to make appropriate interventions based on law and policy.
